release.title: NodeLink v0.1.3 inventory, monitoring, and renewable-credential pilot
release.intended_use: Limited pilot deployment to owned Windows x64 endpoints after the sole repository owner reviewed and accepted the release evidence; this release adds endpoint inventory, monitoring/alerting, a versioned script library, scheduled tasks, and loss-safe agent credential renewal, and is not approved for multi-tenant or high-availability claims.

server.deployment: Deploy source from the exact commit bound to v0.1.3 by the release workflow.

database.migration_policy: Migrations are forward-only across the 0013-0026 chain. Public v0.1.1 databases must pass guarded schema adoption at 0001 before upgrading; v0.1.2 databases upgrade in place from 0012; never edit a revision or perform an in-place downgrade.

protocols.mixed_version_behavior: Agents advertise command-v3 and command-v2 during a staged rollout, but new deployments require command-v3; missing, unknown, and legacy-unversioned capabilities fail closed.

known_limitations: #24: Windows agent and installer artifacts are not Authenticode signed, so SmartScreen or antivirus warnings remain possible.
#66: Roles are global and clients or sites are not authorization tenants; do not market or operate this release as multi-tenant.
#84: Enrollment rate limits, counters, and metrics are process-local; no multi-worker or high-availability protection claim is made.
#126: Empty deployments must bootstrap the first client and site through the existing administrative API before using enrollment.
#76: The local release drill verifies the internal audit chain but has no external immutable audit-anchor receipt to cross-check.
Endpoint inventory, monitoring checks, and alerting are Windows-first; Linux and macOS remain development-only builds with reduced or absent collectors.
Alert email and signed webhook delivery are best-effort with process-local state; there is no multi-worker delivery deduplication or high-availability guarantee.

The 0026-to-0012 rollback rehearsal evaluated the fail-closed compatibility decision freshly against the retained v0.1.2 0012 recovery point; re-decrypting that immutable recovery point requires the operator-held v0.1.2 backup passphrase and reuses the restore verification captured during the v0.1.2 drill rather than repeating the decrypt in-session.

This manifest's backup and rollback evidence is complete, but the full release drill's production HTTPS deployment and Windows canary phases are not part of these records and remain operator tasks before broad rollout.

prerequisites: Pause enrollment, command dispatch, scheduled-task execution, server promotion, and external agent rollout automation.
Verify the current 0012 backup, a fresh pre-upgrade 0026-target backup, manifests, and retained restore evidence against their immutable SHA-256 digests.
Confirm Python 3.12, PostgreSQL, command signing keys, production secrets, trusted-proxy settings, HTTPS public URL, and server-only dashboard API URL are configured.
Verify every release artifact checksum and GitHub build-provenance attestation before execution.
steps: For a v0.1.2 database at 0012, take a verified backup, then run Alembic upgrade through the 0013-0026 chain and confirm the startup revision guard reports 0026 before serving traffic.
For an unversioned public v0.1.1 database, run guarded adoption to 0001 first, then upgrade forward to 0026.
Deploy the server and dashboard together from the workflow-bound v0.1.3 source commit.
Deploy the checksum-verified Windows agent or installer to one owned canary endpoint before expanding the rollout.
Keep v0.1.2 and any failed-state backup unavailable to automatic rollout channels.
verification: Confirm Alembic current reports 0026 and health, readiness, metrics, login, and production configuration checks pass over verified HTTPS.
Confirm a canary endpoint enrolls, renews its agent credential before expiry without losing connectivity, and that a revoked or expired credential fails authentication.
Confirm inventory snapshots, monitoring checks, alert state transitions, email/webhook delivery, script-library execution, and scheduled-task runs behave as expected on the Windows canary.
Confirm heartbeat, audit sequence, expected metric deltas, token revocation, agent revocation, and post-revocation authentication rejection.
Confirm NodeLinkAgent service and installer install, start, stop, restart, and uninstall behavior on Windows, with DPAPI-protected identity and restricted ACLs.

decision_path: Prefer a forward fix while the live database remains at 0026; v0.1.2 is not an in-place server/database rollback target for that schema.
Redeploy v0.1.2 components only when their required 0012 schema and retained artifact digests exactly match a restored deployment.
Before any schema restore, pause rollout and writers, preserve an encrypted failed-state backup, and name the decision maker and exact accepted data-loss window.
Restore the verified 0012 recovery-point backup only after explicit data-loss approval, validate it in isolation, and deploy the exact v0.1.2 server, agent, and installer together.
If the matching backup, artifact, audit, or startup verification fails, keep promotion blocked and continue with a reviewed forward fix.

security_impact.summary: v0.1.3 adds loss-safe agent credential renewal with automatic expiry, endpoint security inventory (Defender, BitLocker, Secure Boot, TPM, local administrators), and monitoring/alerting while preserving fail-closed command verification, production configuration checks, and explicit pilot-only operating limits.
fixed_vulnerabilities: #125: Per-agent bearer credentials now carry server-enforced expiry (migration 0024) and the agent proactively performs loss-safe renewal before expiry, closing the long-lived static-credential limitation from v0.1.2.
Agent-collected security posture (Defender status, BitLocker, Secure Boot, TPM, local Administrators membership) gives operators visibility to detect at-risk endpoints during the pilot.

Dashboard dependency audit is clean: the v0.1.2 development-only lint findings were reassessed and remediated by patch-level lockfile updates (nanoid 3.3.18, postcss 8.5.26, js-yaml 4.3.1, brace-expansion 1.1.18/5.0.9), clearing the transient nanoid advisory that had reached the production tree; npm audit now reports zero production and development vulnerabilities.
new_risks: #24 remains open because Windows artifacts are unsigned and require checksum and provenance verification.
#66 remains open because authorization roles are global rather than tenant scoped.
#84 remains open because enrollment limiting and counters are process local.
Alert email and signed webhook delivery introduce outbound integrations whose secrets and endpoints must be protected and whose delivery state is process local.
Scheduled and recurring task execution broadens the agent's autonomous action surface and must be constrained to reviewed, signed scripts.
operator_actions: Complete the production HTTPS deployment and Windows canary phases of the release drill and retain their evidence before broad rollout; the backup, restore-verification, and rollback-rehearsal evidence referenced here is already published under v0.1.3-evidence.

Because independent second-operator review is not available, the sole release operator must personally verify the complete v0.1.3 evidence index, retained digests, preflight result, and green release checks before tagging.
Protect alert email and webhook secrets, keep enrollment tokens single-use and short-lived, and restrict script-library and scheduled-task content to reviewed, signed scripts.
Use a forward fix by default; do not restore the 0012 recovery point without preserving failed state and explicitly accepting all post-backup data loss.
